**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 300

All Szuriel has ever known is war. In life she was first a champion of justice, then excommunicated from her church for heresy. In response, she slaughtered her way to power until she was crowned empress, then subsequently had every member of her former faith crucified. She went on to wage several brutal wars against neighboring kingdoms until an assassin’s dagger found her heart. Sent to [Abaddon](/Planes.aspx?ID=37), she rose quickly through the ranks of [daemonkind](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=386), and when she saw weakness in the Rider of War, she slew him in battle, claiming his title for herself.

Szuriel appears as a tragic angel with beautiful golden hair, magnificent wings, and polished obsidian eyes that continuously weep blood. She resides in the Cinder Furnace, her corner of Abaddon where instruments of war are forged from the fires of burning souls. Szuriel commands one of the largest standing armies in all of existence, countless daemonic soldiers ready to wage war. All fear oblivion at the hands of Szuriel and her army. The Rider of War is always happy to lend her powers, warriors, and devastating discoveries across the planes. So long as war continues, more souls are pulled into her ever-burning furnace.

There are few lasting cults to Szuriel. She carries a hatred of the gods from her mortal life, but she recognizes religious strife is a wondrous provocation to war. She sees her followers as entirely disposable, allowing them to believe whatever they wish of her so long as they deliver her souls on the ends of their swords. She is symbol of pyrrhic victory, a mocking lie to those promised an angelic reward in the afterlife despite a lifetime of violence. Only oblivion awaits those who serve the Angel of Desolation.

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 244

There are often many differences between diving beings in a pantheon, but sometimes universal concepts can still bind them together. The Hellknight Order of the Godclaw extols the virtues of five gods—Abadar, Asmodeus Iomedae, Irori, and [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=294)—as seen through a particular lens of order and discipline. Though many priests of each individual faith called such views inconceivable or even heretical, the Godclaw’s faithful nevertheless receive divine power from their shared patrons. Due to a simultaneous rise in enlistment by those of orc ancestry in the ranks and endorsement by those faithful to Torag, the god Uirch has replaced the dwarven deity in this pantheon’s ranks. 

Talons of the Godclaw embrace this new unity as they serve the Hellknights, using it to show how adherence and faith in ordered law can bridge gaps thought to be otherwise impassable. They still fully embrace their brethren who still follow the original pantheon of the Godclaw, which continues to empower its members just as strongly as before.

Since their inception, the Hellknight orders have paid little heed to what others think of them. But with new blood also comes a refreshed mandate that older Hellknights might blanch at. When not engaged in battle against the forces of chaos, questing Talons (as they are sometimes more simply called) venture forth from Citadel Dinyar with their grim helmets at their sides and faces bare, allowing them the opportunity to connect to the common folk and teach how the ways of order can improve the lives of all. While unorthodox by Hellknight standards, this approach has led to a significant increase in armiger volunteers all around the world.

**Edicts** be an exemplar of divine order and balance, demonstrate the resilience of your faith by shielding others from chaos, instruct others who show promise in the ways of your order

balance, devotion, discipline, order

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Teki Stronggut (The Rememberer)](/Deities.aspx?ID=505)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 312

Teki Stronggut surprised many scholars in Golarion when she suddenly ascended as a hero-god; most had never heard of her or knew only stories of her failures. Those who personally knew her, however, describe Teki as the kind of person who always ends up achieving her dreams, despite many setbacks and the obvious odds. [Goblins](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=62), [bugbears](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=374), and all kinds of unlikely adventurers were rooting for her, as she remembered and represented them all. “Everyone can become a hero if they put their mind to it,” or so Teki would put it. Teki appears much like she did in life: a goblin with bright yellow skin, a cloak with images of failed heroes she supported in her life, a variety of old weapons and other adventuring junk, and an unremovable grin.

Although often unappreciated by the populace, the Rememberer makes a great effort to have word of unsung heroes reach settlements throughout the Inner Sea. With this knowledge in hand, many of these settlements reach out for help from these unknowns when troubles arise. Her followers are mostly adventurers that get their start with Teki’s help. Once that first job is complete, a hero might gain just enough renown to gain further opportunities. Teki teaches these now-famed heroes to spread the word of other unknown heroes and help continue the chain of renown. Teki’s followers are usually members of guilds, such as monster-slayer guilds or thieves’ guilds, hoping to use the organizations to gain greater recognition. 

Teki Stronggut instructs her followers to leave old weapons, unneeded magic items, or other gear that might help aspiring adventurers start their journey on her altars. These altars tend to have guards to watch over these items, and those who manage to steal from a Stronggut Station earn Teki’s wrath. This wrath manifests as unknown warriors that chase thieves, unfortunate luck on journeys, or even a dwindling of a given thief’s reputation, making acquiring more work difficult. Only once the items are returned or items of similar value are left in their place does Teki let up.

<column gap="tiny">

**Edicts** Remember those whom others forget, help those who need it the most, aid other misfits in their goals

**Anathema** Give up on your cause, punish someone due to failure or incompetence, abandon a fellow adventurer

**Area of Concern**
Haplessness, heroism, the forgotten

Those who personally knew her, however, describe Teki as the kind of person who always ends up achieving her dreams, despite many setbacks and the obvious odds. [Goblins](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=62), [bugbears](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=374), and all kinds of unlikely adventurers were rooting for her, as she remembered and represented them all. “Everyone can become a hero if they put their mind to it,” or so Teki would put it. Teki appears much like she did in life: a goblin with bright yellow skin, a cloak with images of failed heroes she supported in her life, a variety of old weapons and other adventuring junk, and an unremovable grin.

Although often unappreciated by the populace, the Rememberer makes a great effort to have word of unsung heroes reach settlements throughout the Inner Sea. With this knowledge in hand, many of these settlements reach out for help from these unknowns when troubles arise. Her followers are mostly adventurers that get their start with Teki’s help. Once that first job is complete, a hero might gain just enough renown to gain further opportunities. Teki teaches these now-famed heroes to spread the word of other unknown heroes and help continue the chain of renown. Teki’s followers are usually members of guilds, such as monster-slayer guilds or thieves’ guilds, hoping to use the organizations to gain greater recognition. 

Teki Stronggut instructs her followers to leave old weapons, unneeded magic items, or other gear that might help aspiring adventurers start their journey on her altars. These altars tend to have guards to watch over these items, and those who manage to steal from a Stronggut Station earn Teki’s wrath. This wrath manifests as unknown warriors that chase thieves, unfortunate luck on journeys, or even a dwindling of a given thief’s reputation, making acquiring more work difficult. Only once the items are returned or items of similar value are left in their place does Teki let up.

Haplessness, heroism, the forgotten

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

Whether mortals realize it or not, the stars, moons, systems, and galaxies of [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26) all flow in accordance with ancient and fundamental laws set in motion at the dawn of creation. Though magic might pull them from their charted course, even this movement is guided by a force sewn into the fabric of the cosmos. Telastmar, the Cosmic Dyne, is the manifestation of these celestial orbits, keeping the Universe in constant movement. Because this turn of planets and moons controls the tides, Telastmar also holds sway over the oceans, though they curiously seem more concerned with the fish that live in such waters. Adherents claim that Telastmar is the lord and creator of all fish, guiding them on their migrations throughout rivers and seas.

Like most [aeons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=357), Telastmar has more concern with natural laws than mortal lives, but they can be pleased and courted by would-be adherents. Those who study the stars and planets can sometimes find divine inspiration in their elaborate orreries, as the same patterns that underpin the cosmos converge to provide glimpses of the future or fortuitous turns of fate. They also favor space travelers, and a tiny few who have returned to their home planets have claimed sightings of the great starry god-whale swimming alongside their ship.

Most of Telastmar’s worshippers are in academic centers, as the first arbitrator is too esoteric to attract followers from working fishers and sailors. Their mortal cult typically attracts astronomers and travelers who journey between the stars. Those attuned to the tides, stars, and wildlife migrations of the sea, such as migrant Taotake families or the sailors of Minata, sometimes see Telastmar, though most consider them to be a large, powerful spirit. Telastmar has also been known to shine a rare light on those who have become lost in life due to ill fate—a particularly unusual trait in an aeon.

<row gap="medium">

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

When the Universe was young, [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=290) watched mortals as they lived, and when their day arrived, she saw mortality’s love for life push them to defy the cycle and refuse death. Pharasma raised up an asp, reshaping them into a new [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher whose venom—age— would flow through all mortal veins, draining away their memories, their passions, and their vitality, until, when their time comes to its close, they are ready for death’s embrace. 

Teshallas is the Primordial Poison, the usher of age, poison, and all venomous creatures. Though there are many who curse their name, or curse Pharasma’s cruelty for inflicting them on the world, death is not the only gift their venom bears. Their touch allows mortals to grow and mature throughout their lives, gaining the wisdom that comes only through experience. Teshallas is the patron of herbalists, and of poisons refined into medicines that give life instead of take. Their mortal following attracts hedge witches, herbalists, alchemists, and assassins, and these worshippers often maintain small gardens where they cultivate a variety of poisonous plants needed for potion making and alchemy.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[The Devourer (The Star-Eater)](/Deities.aspx?ID=339)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 137

The Devourer is a new deity: an embodiment of ruin on a galactic scale, born from the acts of other deities in ages long past. Thanks to [Gorum](/Deities.aspx?ID=283) and [Torag](/Deities.aspx?ID=294), a sliver of the deity [Rovagug](/Deities.aspx?ID=291) was bound inside Gorum’s armor, turning the deity of war into an eternal prison for the Rough Beast. Inside Gorum, the sliver festered, changing and warping into something new. Following the events of the Godsrain and Gorum’s demise, the sliver managed to escape its prison and ascend into the cosmos as its own being, the Devourer.

The Star-Eater has no concept of worship, its nascent following, or even that it exists among a pantheon of other deities. It’s a being of pure primal force that seeks the fruition of complete universal entropy. The only thing the Devourer wants is for everything to end, and its every action is in pursuit of that total goal. It embodies devastation and undoing at a level that goes beyond most mortal comprehension, moving beyond everyday events that more personify Rovagug’s destructive nature. The Devourer represents events that destroy stars and entire worlds. While most people have little understanding of the concept of a black hole or supernova, the Devourer is a being who seeks to enact such events throughout the galaxy. 

Though few in divine circles have had time to truly comprehend the ramifications of the Devourer’s birth— or more accurately, its emancipation from the prison of Gorum’s armor. Countless cults have already begun to form around intangible apocalyptic visions seen in dreams or from the ongoing ramifications of the Godsrain itself. So far, only a handful of these cults have blossomed on Golarion, as the Devourer seems instinctively apprehensive of the world that acts as a prison to Rovagug. The same cannot be said for worlds beyond Golarion, and even nearby worlds such as Akiton and Castrovel are already beginning to see the burgeoning of destructive cults of the Devourer. Such cults are almost entirely as damaging as they are selfdestructive, with splintered leadership and rash actions often leading to infighting that quickly spreads out to encompass communities or entire nations in its wake. 

The Devourer has no relationships with other deities, as it cannot even recognize the existence of other divine beings as anything more than impediments to its cause. It appears as though the Devourer seeks to give Golarion a wide berth, somehow instinctively fearing the cage that contains the Rough Beast. One other deity has taken particular interest in the Devourer: [Groetus](/Deities.aspx?ID=38). The God of the End Times is an inscrutable entity, but it’s said that when the Devourer escaped from its prison within Gorum, the eyes of the vast moon that is Groetus shifted, as though its attention was momentarily held by the birth of such an apocalyptic entity. What this means is the stuff of metaphysical debate.

<column gap="tiny">

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[The Green Mother (The Feasting Flower)](/Deities.aspx?ID=453)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 306

The Eldest of carnivorous plants, intrigue, and seduction, the Green Mother personifies the raw thrill and desire found throughout nature. Lush plants that entice prey only to kill with barbs or toxins lie within her authority, as do lustful acts and whispered secrets occurring in wild terrain. Her seductive form shifts from that of a beautiful fey such as a nymph to incorporating natural lures like sweet-smelling flowers and graceful verdant tresses. Just as the Green Mother’s form constantly changes, her mood shifts from mercurial temptress to indifferent poisoner. No matter her form or attitude, the Green Mother is among the canniest of the Eldest, and she maintains several loyal agents who keep her well informed about goings-on in the First World and beyond. This information fuels her intrigues among the Eldest, and they all believe it wisest to keep on the Green Mother’s good side lest their secrets be seductively whispered into the ears of their enemies.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[The Lady of the North Star (Mother of Secrets)](/Deities.aspx?ID=303)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=237) pg. 21

A goddess whose name has been lost to time (or purposefully obscured), the secretive Lady of the North Star is referred to only by her countless epithets. Despite the efforts of Pharasma's faithful to scrub the Lady's name from the annals of history, a few scattered sects still worship her and transmit her teachings. Their ranks are often closed to outsiders, and their initiation rituals are arduous and famously cryptic. In spite of the Lady of the North Star's love for secrecy, she has one famous weakness: her empathy for those nearing death. She has been known to take pity on those afflicted with incurable curses and ailments of all kinds, appearing to prospective followers through dreams and visions. There, she presents them with a final challenge: to uncover her lost path to immortality before their time runs out.

 According to legend, the Lady of the North Star once descended to the mortal world, disguising herself as a human. She witnessed firsthand the horrors of mortality as her newfound friends grew old and weak with time, with even the strongest warriors ultimately succumbing to illness and infirmity. Her frigid heart was moved. She took such pity on the mortal peoples of the world that she conspired to create a forbidden ritual, strong enough to grant immortality to any mortal skilled enough to execute it. She split the mysterious ritual into nine stages, hiding the nine fragments across the land of Tian Xia.

 The truth of the ritual has been lost to time, but all her sects agree that upon successful completion, the performer will ascend to join the Lady and her mysterious court of immortals that lies far beyond the stars to the North, shielded from mortal eyes and cloaked in impenetrable darkness. There, the wintry night is cold enough to freeze even the wheels of time, preserving her followers' immortality for all eternity.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[The Lantern King (The Laughing Lie)](/Deities.aspx?ID=455)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 306

Although the Lantern King most often appears as a floating ball of light surrounded by runes that form a delicate crown, the Eldest of laughter, mischief, and transformation has taken on a dizzying array of figures. He often adopts alternate shapes to play pranks, and even other Eldest are not immune to his mischievous scheming. Although he insists his pranks are intended only for levity and to bring down imperious snobs, the chaos he creates in the name of good-natured fun is, to his targets, embarrassing at best and sometimes outright lethal. The Lantern King wanders the First World more than other Eldest, and he can be encountered in crowded markets and lonely byways alike. He is frequently accompanied by the Witchmarket, a traveling caravan of entertainers and merchants that serves as his court.

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 306

The Eldest of loneliness, sadness, and forgotten things, the Lost Prince spends most of his time brooding in the throne room of his crumbling tower. Although his precise origin is a hotly debated issue, the Lost Prince is known to hail from a place other than the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=35). The melancholy lord doesn’t speak of his home, and in fact he doesn’t speak much at all, as he’s prone to bouts of depression powerful enough to leach color from his surroundings and press his coterie of followers into respectful silence. Appearing as a gaunt, pale human man dressed in black finery, the Lost Prince bears vivid red runes on his brow and on the backs of his hands. He is studiously neutral in the schemes of the other Eldest, which makes his opinions and his favor particularly valuable.

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

The Pale Horse stalks the banks of the River of Souls. This has been true for eons, though few things are immune to change, and the story of the Pale Horse is no exception. Long ago, the stories say, a [daemon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=386) traveled the pathways between the planes, consuming the souls of the dead before they reached the Lady of Graves. He appeared as a silent white stallion, and his name was the Pale Horse. Now, they speak of a [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher who guards mortal souls while they journey into the afterlife, hunting any who dare steal from the River of Souls. His name is the Pale Horse, and he serves the Gray Lady.

The Pale Horse is the usher of duty and burden, but where once his craven whims held him captive, now he fulfills the divine charge of Pharasma, obligated to her service until the day he has saved half as many souls as he damned in a previous life. He is the Lash and the Plough, worshipped by bounty hunters, servants, beleaguered workers, risen daemons like himself, and by those who have been wronged. His wrath is legendary, though many psychopomps fear his vengeance will turn on the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39) once his sentence is complete.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Monitor Demigods
](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=12)

**Anathema** Break an oath, cower from combat, damage or destroy a soul, show mercy to those who betray you

Beasts of burden, duty, revenge

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[The Pandemonia](/Deities.aspx?ID=370)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 239

Some people just want to throw the world into chaos, whether on a smaller scale through vexing pranks or on a larger scale by embracing complete anarchy. Adherents to the Pandemonia venerate the most confounding of extraplanar entities, ones who refuse to be bound by order and decorum to do whatever they want whenever they want. Some claim that their acts are all in good fun, but they often don’t take the feelings of those they trick into account. Others know full well the consequences of their actions and simply don’t care who they hurt. As befitting such a chaotic covenant, there is hardly any conformity of beliefs or methods within its ranks, making it almost more of a philosophy (albeit a rather disorganized one) than anything else.

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 240

Across Golarion, major wars have changed the course of history. Some have altered the political make-up of a region, with nations rising and falling. Others have left physical scars on the landscape that force citizens to relocate or change their ways of life. From stealthy scouts pointing the way to generals making plans, most soldiers understand that military strength comes from unity and communication. Followers of the Readied Strike hold that knowledge as personal faith, sometimes hard-won by those who have fallen in past battles. These covenant followers study historical battles, develop new strategies, and share them with their allies to better stand against their foes. They are also constantly honing their martial skills, with a few under the direct tutelage of intelligent magic weapons inhabited by the ghosts of deceased warriors.

battlefield tactics, communication, strategic planning, training regimens

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Thremyr (The First Jarl)](/Deities.aspx?ID=497)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Thremyr is a mountainous, ancient being with a long, full beard and hair of salt, a stout body of frigid ice, and a set of chilling blue gems for eyes. The earliest available records of the god tell the tale of his awakening during Earthfall as the meteorite landed on [Golarion](/Rules.aspx?ID=3298), tearing open the Inner Sea. Anything prior to that is currently undocumented or lost as a result of this cataclysmic event.

The First Jarl’s following is comprised almost entirely of frost giants. They claim that he is their unwitting creator, born of the glaciers and icebergs that sloughed off his body when he fell into the Steaming Sea. Initially, he saw these frost giants as small and unflattering mockeries of himself and chased them away. However, they eventually returned with tributes and praise for him. It was then that he finally decided to accept these frost giants as his own.

Though Thremyr is usually in a deep slumber, his followers go to great lengths to keep him happy, conducting raids on cities and villages to give the valuables they plunder to him as tributes. Altars and buildings used to store these ill-gotten gains are always distinctly marked with the image of a frozen blue gemstone. It’s well known and accepted by even his worshippers that he cares very little for them. It’s Thremyr’s love of treasures that keep them in his good graces, blessing those who consistently give great bounties with answered prayers and potent ancient magic.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Thuskchoon (Everglutton)](/Deities.aspx?ID=586)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 320

Thuskchoon is a towering slug with numerous limbs and ravenous maws that slithers through the [Outer Rifts](/Planes.aspx?ID=45), consuming all that he finds. In the wake of his near-mindless devastation, his mouths leaves swaths of disgusting tar. Sometimes, Everglutton stumbles across a portal to another plane, though these changes of scenery barely register with the qlippoth lord. He simply continues to indulge his insatiable hunger, uncaring of what (or who) he eats. 

Devotees of Thuskchoon expect little from their patron, but they crave the hidden knowledge sometimes revealed by his (and others’) wanton destruction. Scholars, pirates, and archaeologists are counted among his cultists, cloaking their endeavors under the guise of academia. They seek out ancient ruins to plunder, usually breaking timeworn architecture and antiquities in their heedless searching. Occasionally, an Everglutton cult gains enough power to direct Thuskchoon’s movements in small ways, sending the qlippoth lord to specific areas they believe conceal mighty secrets. Some worshippers are killed in the resulting demolition, but this never slows their fellow devotees’ pursuits, nor does it bother the indifferent Thuskchoon.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Titivilus (The Scrivener)](/Deities.aspx?ID=530)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 314

Upon the backs of all beholden to him, Titivilus scratches the record of [Hell](/Planes.aspx?ID=42) with long claws. His is a slender form, almost like a [human](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=64) man stretched well beyond his typical proportions, with skin the color of the deep purples of a sunset. Nine hands, each with nine fingers, transcribe every word spoken within the rings in illustrious longhand and great detail, down to the tones and rhythms. Steel is a crude tool for change; the Scrivening Count would crumble empires with but a whisper. A spear and shield may break a body, but lies, propaganda, rhetoric, and truth manipulate the hearts and minds that drive the hands.

Politicians, barristers, poets, and the like count on Titivilus for guidance on how to manipulate the masses. In exchange, they give stories and rarefied texts. With these, Titivilus has composed the most comprehensive and unbiased history of each plane from the beginning of time to ever exist.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Tjasse (Lord of Talons)](/Deities.aspx?ID=498)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Tjasse, the father of [Skode](/Deities.aspx?ID=239), is the [cloud giant](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3015) god and lord of rocs, wind, and high mountain peaks. He is credited for taming rocs to serve cloud giants and possessing shapeshifting abilities second only to [Skrymir](/Deities.aspx?ID=496) (much to his chagrin). Stories of his incredible arrogance precede him and most of his accolades, closely followed by cautionary tales of those unfortunate enough to have provoked his ire. The only thing that surpasses his vanity is his love for Skode, and the only thing greater than the wrath incurred by those who cross him is the destructive force he unleashes upon those who wrong his daughter. The Lord of Talons is a colossal being, dwarfing many members of the giant pantheon in comparison. He is always described as strikingly beautiful, though the exact details of his appearance change frequently.

Followers of Tjasse are often those who call the mountains their home, as well as roc tamers and riders who look to him to ensure the winds are in their favor when they take flight. There are a few who turn to him when seeking power to exact revenge, trusting that he understands and shares their need for decisive retaliation.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Giant Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=26)

**Edicts** Only ever hunt birds for food, aggressively oppose those who do not have your best interest at heart, protect your children at all cost

**Anathema** Harm birds for sport or via negligence, bow down to your oppressor, show mercy to anyone who wronged your child

Giant birds, mountain peaks, pride

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Tolte Coatl (The Crafter of Knowledge)](/Deities.aspx?ID=415)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 302

Tolte Coatl (TOLL-teh coh-AHtl) is the youngest of the tribunal, but sometimes seen as the leader of three. While he is always looking to help mortals and share righteous ideals with them, Tolte Coatl is more concerned with matters of the mind than the more physical pursuits of his siblings. He teaches that knowledge isn’t simply accumulated all at once, it’s slowly built up, like a home being built one brick at a time; knowledge must generally be built upon itself. One can’t know how to cook for oneself until they know how to create a fire. Tolte Coatl encourages patience with learning and acquiring new skills. He also encourages sharing knowledge when it can help others. As such, he sometimes grants his followers gifts of small pieces of vital information that can help unlock new collections of knowledge, such as a vital component to a new invention or a portion of an alchemical formula.

Tolte Coatl also encourages regular journeys, as a means of acquiring new knowledge, but also to refresh the mind. A mind that remains in one place too long can grow stale, clouded by the familiar. Journeys are also new experiences, whether they can teach a person or not, and novel experiences tend to make new memories. Associations with powerful memories can help a person, and many times, hide lessons that a person can discover upon reflection. While Tolte Coatl generally distances himself from combat, he and his followers will intercede to protect knowledge. Tolte Coatl appears as an auwaz [coatl](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=382), a coatl known for aiding others on their journeys. His servitors include guides, inventors, and teachers. Tolte Coatl’s symbol is a coatl’s wing raining down stars.

<column gap="tiny">

**Edicts** Encourage others to join you on travels, offer to teach those who are genuinely eager to learn, ask others to share their tales

**Anathema** Alter the memory of another, deny someone who genuinely wishes to journey with you and would not harm you

**Area of Concern**
Knowledge, memories, migration

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Torag (Father of Creation)](/Deities.aspx?ID=294)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 102

The head of the dwarven pantheon is the most visible of the dwarven deities, to the extent that Torag is the only dwarven deity most non-dwarves know of. While the other dwarven gods represent specific areas of dwarven life and culture, thus forming an expansive and comprehensive dwarven pantheon, Torag’s areas of concern are those most central to dwarven society. In his own family, Torag models the values of community and protection that have cemented deep-rooted relationships among dwarven clans. His focus on strategy and tactical acumen centers on protection, reflected in dwarves’ impenetrable fortresses and conservative military tactics, including their willingness to use offensive maneuvers as a form of defense. He also represents the forge: the creation of fine works from raw materials, practice and mastery of a craft, and pride in one’s work. His purview extends even to those activities that feed the forge and dwarven artisanship, such as mining the earth for raw ore and gemstones. Torag’s oversight over these core concepts has secured his place at the head of the dwarven pantheon for ages. It was Torag who sent the dwarves on their legendary Quest for Sky during the Age of Darkness, and his worship was long-established even then. Indeed, among dwarves, Torag is often called the Father of Creation.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Gods of the Inner Sea](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=1)

**Edicts** be honorable and forthright, keep your word, respect the forge, serve your people

**Anathema** tell lies or cheat someone, intentionally create inferior works, show continued mercy to the enemies of your people when such enemies prove they are undeserving

**Area of Concern**
forge, protection, and strategy

**Pantheons**
[Demon Bringers](/Deities.aspx?ID=230), [Dwarven Pantheon](/Deities.aspx?ID=196), [Good Neighbors](/Deities.aspx?ID=368), [Stone's Blood](/Deities.aspx?ID=382), [The Godclaw](/Deities.aspx?ID=198), [The Laborer's Bastion](/Deities.aspx?ID=253), [Wheels Of Innovation](/Deities.aspx?ID=385)

</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Deities/Torag.png" />
</column>

</row>
<title level="2">Devotee Benefits</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**[Divine Attribute](/Backgrounds.aspx?ID=132)**
Constitution or Wisdom

**Divine Font** [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148)

**Divine Sanctification** can choose holy

**Divine Skill** [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37)

**Favored Weapon** [Warhammer](/Weapons.aspx?ID=403)

**Domains** [Creation](/Domains.aspx?ID=68), [Earth](/Domains.aspx?ID=73), [Family](/Domains.aspx?ID=74), [Protection](/Domains.aspx?ID=90)

**[Alternate Domains](/Rules.aspx?ID=802)** [Duty](/Domains.aspx?ID=108), [Metal](/Domains.aspx?ID=112)

**Cleric Spells**

- **1st**
[Mindlink](/Spells.aspx?ID=1603)

- **3rd**
[Earthbind](/Spells.aspx?ID=1506)

- **4th**
[Creation](/Spells.aspx?ID=1477)

</column><title level="2">Divine Intercession</title>

Torag makes his pleasure or displeasure known through unsubtle signs.

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 47 <sup>2.0</sup>

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Boon** Torag repairs your equipment so you may continue your vigil. Once, a shield, weapon, or other item you hold or are wearing recovers all of its Hit Points. The item’s Hardness doubles for 1 minute. Torag can grant this boon just as the item would have been destroyed, preventing the item’s destruction. Occasionally, he grants this boon to restore an item important to dwarven history that has already been fully destroyed.

**Moderate Boon** You are counted as family among Torag and his followers. You gain the effects of a single [dwarf ancestry feat](/Feats.aspx?Traits=54) of Torag’s choice, even if you are not a dwarf, as long as you maintain Torag’s blessing.

**Major Boon** Standing watch or guarding a location counts as resting for you, preventing you from being [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) due to lack of rest as long as you stand watch for at least 6 hours a day. You can recover your Focus Points (if you have them) by standing guard in addition to any other options you have available. When on guard, you gain a +4 status bonus to Perception to notice ambushes and other dangers approaching. As long as you are holding a shield, you are always [Defending](/Activities.aspx?ID=2) during exploration without needing to move at half your travel speed, and you can perform another exploration activity as well. While you are using a shield, its Hardness increases by 5.
</column>

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Curse** Shoddy artisanship makes itself known. Whenever an item you’re using takes damage, it is [broken](/Conditions.aspx?ID=2).

**Moderate Curse** You must prove your skills at a craft by providing your own equipment. You gain item bonuses only from items you make yourself.

**Major Curse** You are forever cast out from your home. Members of your community have their attitudes towards you shift two steps worse, meaning those who used to be [helpful](/Conditions.aspx?ID=21) are now [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25), those who were [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18) are now [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=40), and all others are now [hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23). This doesn’t necessarily result in violence, but hostile community members generally seek your permanent exile.
</column>

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Treasures Of The Eternal Delve](/Deities.aspx?ID=374)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 241

The endless tunnels and caverns of the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=30) host a multitude of burrowing creatures, beings made of stone, and those who continually excavate precious gems from the surrounding rock. This near-ceaseless labor generates a kind of divine power that those who respect the soil can give their faith to, in the form of this covenant. They appreciate the dichotomy between the sheer strength of stone and the sometimes delicate nature of crystals and gems, and the fact that the latter is often more valuable than the former. But these worshippers know that all things that come from the earth have their own beauty. Followers of the Treasures of the Eternal Delve also respect the importance of stability and safety when searching for these riches, as many of them could be easily crushed by a collapsing tunnel or falling slab of rock.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Trelmarixian (The Lysogenic Prince)](/Deities.aspx?ID=393)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 300

Before his mortal death, Trelmarixian had already destroyed an entire world. Born a [daemonic](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=386)-blooded [tiefling](/Traits.aspx?ID=258), his hatred of those around him was an allconsuming hunger, and he never knew peace. During an eclipse, he performed a ritual so powerful it mummified every living creature on his world, and his heart was finally full. Dying from starvation but elated by his success, Trelmarixian heard a voice call out to him. The voice mocked him, exclaiming all he’d accomplished was insignificant compared to what awaited him next. Trelmarixian’s last mortal memory was of staring into an eclipse.

Lyutheria, the original Rider of Famine, was impressed by Trelmarixian’s conquest and took him on as her apprentice, fatally underestimating his ambitions. After Trelmarixian learned all he could from his master, he devoured her and assumed her title.

Trelmarixian appears as sickly man with three snapping jackal heads and putrid, membranous flesh that is constantly dripping and sloughing off his body. As the Rider of Famine, Trelmarixian ushers in oblivion slowly, watching mortals waste away as their bodies turn against them. He spreads cancer by touch, inciting cells to rebellion, and his breath causes outbreaks of hives and asthma attacks in those nearby. He aligns himself with [Szuriel](/Deities.aspx?ID=136) to see that soldiers never make it home to reap their fields, leaving crops to rot on the vine. He collaborates with [Apollyon](/Deities.aspx?ID=134) to spread diseases from livestock, rendering butchers’ larders barren. Trelmarixian has little trust for [Charon](/Deities.aspx?ID=135), however, certain that the oldest Rider is hiding secrets. 

Trelmarixian’s ambition was not sated by attaining a revered place among the Apocalypse Riders. He buries a piece of himself within each of his daemonic servitors, allowing him control over them. As a result, his psyche is constantly deluged by voices from his servants, and with only great focus can he hush them. Yet there is always a single voice that cannot be silenced, the same that spoke to him before his death. That voice continues to speak to him, promising a future of devastation still to come.

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 302

Tyrants, greedy landlords, and corrupt governments suck their constituents dry in pursuit of their own fortunes, and Tresmalvos welcomes them all to the harbinger’s water-logged, rotting bosom. The Cistern Queen is the unquestioned ruler of her domain, a sprawling labyrinth of dark sewer tunnels decorated with the befouled trappings of the wealthy. Though the indulgent wealthy do her work without knowing it, Tresmalvos is often petitioned by those of lowlier stations (such as rat catchers) in the hopes of inverting the current power structure. Occasionally, the Cistern Queen will grant such a request (usually via her swarms of filthy rats), elevating a worshipper to a higher status, only to entice them into acting the same way as their former oppressors.

Tresmalvos appears as a drowned [elf](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=60) wearing a rusted iron crown, with piercing yellow eyes, a rat’s tail, and other ever-shifting features. As a stark contrast to their physical appearance, her voice is sweet, melodious, and implacable.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Tsukiyo (Prince of the Moon)](/Deities.aspx?ID=317)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 160

Tsukiyo has always been considered a complicated god in Tian Xia, constantly changing like the phases of the moon. As with any other god, the Prince of the Moon is understood in different ways depending on time and place, which he views as mortal concerns rather than something he should control. Tsukiyo has little impact on state functions or annual events, but his influence runs deep in the daily lives and perspectives of Minkai. He is the Prince of the Moon, representing the night and the natural changes everyone experiences in life.

 For the average person, Tsukiyo is worshipped quietly through self-reflection and meditation. In recent decades, his story has become primarily about trauma and transformation, where the boisterous lover of Shizuru is murdered out of jealousy, then resurrected as a distant and contemplative man. It is thought that his death and return caused him to drift from his old life, making him a wandering guide for social outcasts and lost spirits. Based on this view, the most devout of his followers join a priesthood dedicated to counseling and social support for the misunderstood. Priests of Tsukiyo often travel widely for the first five years of their training, observing the diversity of the world's peoples. With the understanding that there are no quick fixes to prejudice or exclusion, they eventually settle in a community where they believe they can provide stability and steady guidance.

 In the ancient records of Minkai, there is an entry that suggests Tsukiyo's older brother, Fumeiyoshi, was not solely driven by jealousy over the depth of Tsukiyo and Shizuru's relationship. Fumeiyoshi truly believed that he and his brother must have something in common, and that what was good and warm about Tsukiyo was ultimately just a reflection of Shizuru's light. Although there was no proof of this, his resentment and jealousy ultimately combined and led to him murdering his younger brother. For this reason, the annual Jukuk-o festival is held every winter solstice to not only show devotion to Tsukiyo and practice self-reflection, but also to consider the harm caused by unfounded judgments. Beyond Minkai, Tsukiyo is an important patron to samsarans, who seek enlightenment through reincarnation and learning from the past.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Tian Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=16)

**Edicts** provide aid and counsel without judgment to those who seek help, help the dead find their rest, amplify or help speak for the powerless and demonized

**Anathema** harm another out of envy, force aid on those who do not want it, inflict harmful mental effects on others as punishment, knowingly hurt the innocent, commit murder

**Area of Concern**
jade, the moon, spirits

**Pantheons**
[Cosmic Caravan](/Deities.aspx?ID=377), [Guardians Of The Sacred Self](/Deities.aspx?ID=379)

</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>
<title level="2">Devotee Benefits</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**[Divine Attribute](/Backgrounds.aspx?ID=132)**
Constitution or Intelligence

**Divine Font** [Heal](/Spells.aspx?ID=148)

**Divine Sanctification** can choose holy

**Divine Skill** [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44)

**Favored Weapon** [Spear](/Weapons.aspx?ID=365)

**Domains** [Disorientation](/Domains.aspx?ID=105), [Moon](/Domains.aspx?ID=84), [Repose](/Domains.aspx?ID=116), [Soul](/Domains.aspx?ID=118)

**[Alternate Domains](/Rules.aspx?ID=802)** [Change](/Domains.aspx?ID=102)

**Cleric Spells**

- **1st**
[Soothe](/Spells.aspx?ID=1678)

- **4th**
[Peaceful Bubble](/Spells.aspx?ID=1624)

- **5th**
[Hallucination](/Spells.aspx?ID=1551)

</column><title level="2">Divine Intercession</title>

Ever mercurial, the Prince of the Moon gives his blessings rarely and somewhat spontaneously. An understanding soul, he is as slow to curse as he is to bless.

**Source** [Gods & Magic - Web Supplement](/Sources.aspx?ID=19) pg. 9

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Boon** Tsukiyo’s simplest show of gratitude is a gift of clarity. Once, when you roll a failure on a saving throw against a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effect, you get a critical success instead. Tsukiyo typically grants this boon against a particularly consequential mental effect.

**Moderate Boon** Tsukiyo watches over you and guards your sleep. You are guaranteed a peaceful night’s rest no matter what conditions you are sleeping in. Even nightmare and similar abilities can’t disrupt your sleep unless they come from a deity, artifact, or similarly powerful source.

**Major Boon** Tsukiyo shares some of his own nature and can lead a favored soul back along the same path he has walked. The next time you would die, you are instead instantly restored to full health and lose any negative conditions you have.
</column>

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Curse** Those who offend Tsukiyo find that light actively shuns them. You lose any low-light vision or darkvision you have, and you treat all light levels as one step lower.

**Moderate Curse** If Tsukiyo is particularly offended by someone, they may find themselves lost in delusions of moonlight. When attempting to navigate or find something at night, if you roll a success or critical success on your Perception check, [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) check, or other check to do so, you get a failure instead.

**Major Curse** When Tsukiyo truly loses patience with someone, he forces them to experience the hardships of others firsthand. Whenever you touch another creature or another creature touches you, you immediately gain any negative curses, diseases, and conditions they are suffering. These effects spread to you even when you Strike another creature or a creature Strikes you.
</column>

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Uirch (The Bulwark)](/Deities.aspx?ID=560)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

In life, Uirch was a follower of [Sarenrae](/Deities.aspx?ID=292) and a warpriest in the Burning Sun hold under warlord Mahja. He became a god upon usurping the tyrannical god Lanishra. Like [Mahja](/Deities.aspx?ID=557), Uirch has incorporated much of Sarenrae’s teachings into his own, but his primary goals are to protect those who cannot protect themselves and prevent tyranny from taking root. Prior to his ascension, Uirch spent much of his time learning various ways to protect people, both physically and mentally. He also studied the most impactful preventive measures to ensure people wouldn’t need protection in the first place. One such measure that Uirch strongly advocates is inhibiting tyranny from taking hold. He encourages leaders to be strong and benevolent, but also to ensure that there exists a system to keep a watchful eye out for those in power who might exceed the duties of their station and become tyrants. He instructs all his followers to do the same, and there are already several small orc holds adopting his philosophies and placing his priests in positions as guides and counselors.

Now, Uirch the Bulwark spends much of his time passing on knowledge to his followers, both directly and indirectly. As a newly ascended god, he has not yet created a strongly codified system of rules and guidelines. He asks that his followers stamp out abuses of power, protect the innocent, and ensure that they remain ready and capable of facing whatever trials and dangers might assail them or those who turn to them for protection.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Ulon (The Web)](/Deities.aspx?ID=412)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 302

Ulon is one of the most mysterious gods from ancient Azlant society.

A god of conspiracy, isolation, and manipulation, Ulon believed that uncovering truths and sowing mistrust and questions that distracted society from the on-going underground machinations of the Web. Knowing that truth and lies are often found in the same vein, Ulon encouraged picking apart lies to reveal the truth beneath them, pushing followers toward a greater concept known as the All-Truth.

Ulon encourages followers to never blindly accept anything as truth. Instead, the Web supports questioning everything. Ulon was and is still largely considered an urban myth by most beyond the few cells who venerate the Web. Few have ever heard the name, and those who have dismiss talk of Ulon as fantastic tales or conspiratorial rumors. Ulon teaches that all things are connected and that by pulling the right strings, one can manipulate the strings of power and make authority one’s puppet.

While Ulon’s following declined significantly after Earthfall, the few faithful who survived struggled to carry and pass along Ulon’s teachings. These followers continued to live in the shadows of society, undermining authority and bringing new cells into The Web’s network. Followers have been surfacing more publicly in recent years, spreading whispers of something on the horizon. Whether this is a sign of Ulon’s machinations working behind the scenes or a predicted event finally coming to fruition is yet to be seen, but Ulon’s name coming up in regular conversation is not a thing to be taken lightly.

<row gap="medium">

<traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Faith in Urazra is relatively new, only coming about within the past few centuries. However, his following has grown rapidly among the young [stone](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3012) and [marsh giants](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3011) of a more violent incline. Even in the short amount of time that he has been a part of the giant pantheon, there have already been countless tales of his barbarity. In all of them, he is described as a blood-splattered stone giant man with a burly build, pauldrons fashioned from deer or moose skulls, and a jagged onyx-black greatsword with a length that rivals his height.

Followers of the Breaker of Bones are known as the [Bear](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=370) Cult, a faith that is quickly and effectively spreading thanks to their charismatic preachers and barbarians claiming their powerful rage is from the god himself. Many stone giant warriors are among his worshippers, drawn in by his promise of unholy might, resilience, and an immunity to pain for those who enact ruthless violence and conduct sacrifices of flesh in his name. They tout ferocity and strength as aspects more important than the works, knowledge, or history that their elders taught them, causing the cult to be met with great enmity from other stone giants.

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Urgathoa (The Pallid Princess)](/Deities.aspx?ID=295)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 106

The chosen of Urgathoa do not dread the flaws of mortal flesh, such as aging, disease, or even death, for so long as they indulge in excess above all else, their goddess offers eternal freedom from such fickle constraints. Urgathoa herself was once a mortal woman who challenged and rejected the tenets of deities whose followers expected mindless conformity, temperance, and restraint. Why would the gods craft Golarion into a near-endless buffet abundant with pleasures of the body and mind if the living weren’t destined to feast from it? Urgathoa so loved satiating her life’s appetites that in death, she spat in the face of [Pharasma’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) judgment, murdered the psychopomp assigned to aid her transition to the afterlife, and tore herself from the Boneyard with a feat of will that not only returned her to the Material Plane but also transformed her into the first divine undead creature.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Gods of the Inner Sea](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=1)

**Edicts** become undead upon death, create or protect the undead, sate your appetites

**Anathema** deny your appetites, destroy undead of no harm to you, sacrifice your life

**Area of Concern**
disease, gluttony, and undeath

**Pantheons**
[Children Of The Night](/Deities.aspx?ID=376)

</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">
<image src="/images/Deities/Urgathoa.png" />
</column>

</row>
<title level="2">Devotee Benefits</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**[Divine Attribute](/Backgrounds.aspx?ID=132)**
Constitution or Wisdom

**Divine Font** [Harm](/Spells.aspx?ID=146)

**Divine Sanctification** must choose unholy

**Divine Skill** [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40)

**Favored Weapon** [Scythe](/Weapons.aspx?ID=394)

**Domains** [Indulgence](/Domains.aspx?ID=79), [Magic](/Domains.aspx?ID=82), [Might](/Domains.aspx?ID=83), [Undeath](/Domains.aspx?ID=97)

**[Alternate Domains](/Rules.aspx?ID=802)** [Decay](/Domains.aspx?ID=104), [Plague](/Domains.aspx?ID=115), [Swarm](/Domains.aspx?ID=120)

**Cleric Spells**

- **1st**
[Goblin Pox](/Spells.aspx?ID=1545)

- **2nd**
[False Vitality](/Spells.aspx?ID=1523)

- **7th**
[Mask of Terror](/Spells.aspx?ID=1595)

</column><title level="2">Divine Intercession</title>

Urgathoa interferes in mortal affairs to fuel her own self-gratification and obsession with observing new sensations.

**Source** [Gods & Magic](/Sources.aspx?ID=17) pg. 49 <sup>2.0</sup>

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Boon** You feast on the spoils of life and death. You gain the benefits of the [irongut goblin heritage](/Heritages.aspx?ID=17), regardless of your ancestry. If you already have this heritage, the circumstance bonus increases to +4.

**Moderate Boon** Urgathoa blesses you as one of her children. You gain negative healing.

**Major Boon** When you contract contagions, you experience fever dreams filled with insight. Once afflicted with a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), you gain the effects of [_foresight_](/Spells.aspx?ID=127) with yourself as the target until no longer afflicted with any disease.
</column>

<column gap="tiny">
**Minor Curse** You must overindulge or partake in forbidden feasts before you find yourself even remotely sated. You need to eat 20 times as much food as normal to avoid [starvation](/Rules.aspx?ID=537), though you always feel hungry regardless of how much you eat. If you dine on the flesh and blood of sapient creatures, you need to eat only the normal amount of such meals and your hunger abates.

**Moderate Curse** Urgathoa cuts you off from positive energy without granting you the blessing of undeath. You are harmed by positive effects and don’t recover Hit Points from them, as if you were an undead or had negative healing, but you are still harmed by negative effects as normal.

**Major Curse** Urgathoa teaches you that pointless lives in slavery to death and morality are bound to end in tragedy. You develop an incurable wasting disease that leaves you [clumsy 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=3), [enfeebled 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13), and unable to move except by [Crawling](/Actions.aspx?ID=76). This disease never progresses further to kill you, but it passes to your friends and loved ones merely by sight, wasting them away unto death before your eyes and causing them to rise as undead to haunt you.
</column>

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Uskyeria (The Saintly Slumberer)](/Deities.aspx?ID=485)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Whether consciously or not, every successful hunter knows that a balance must be struck between observation and action, preparation and instinct, life and death. Taking more from the land than what is sustainable entices predators to be bolder, possibly turning the hunter into the hunted. Those who seek harmony while they live off the land give deference to Uskyeria, who urges her followers to embrace this equilibrium. Death is a natural part of life. Predators hunt prey. Those who are best suited to do so will survive. Those who don’t still feed the circle of life.

Appearing as a gigantic red [bear](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=370) with gold-streaked fur, Uskyeria is said to have originated in the far north of Avistan, between the realms currently known as Irrisen and the Sarkoris Scar. Also known as the Saintly Slumberer, this [agathion](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=216) empyreal lord’s invisible servitors bring restful sleep to both predator and prey, so they can awake refreshed upon the morn to begin the cycle anew. Insomniacs far from nature who seek balance in their own lives also pray to Uskyeria. Seeing their hunt for strength and balance just as deserving, she sometimes blesses them with the rest they so desperately need.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Empyreal Lords](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=10)

**Edicts** Preserve and protect natural resources, respect the animals you kill and their spirits, sleep as long as you need to in order to have strength for the day

**Anathema** Kill animals for reasons other than self-defense or sustenance, over-hunt the land, prevent others from getting as much sleep as they want

**Area of Concern**
Hunting, insomniacs, prudence, slumber

</column>

</column>

<column gap="medium">

</column>

</row>
<title level="2">Devotee Benefits</title>

<column gap="tiny">

**Divine Sanctification** can choose holy

**Favored Weapon** [Scimitar](/Weapons.aspx?ID=393)

**Domains** [Death](/Domains.aspx?ID=70), [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=85), [Vigil](/Domains.aspx?ID=123), [Zeal](/Domains.aspx?ID=100)

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Ussharassim (The Spurring Scar)](/Deities.aspx?ID=531)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 314

From a bacchanal gallery of gloried names remembered fondly, Ussharassim bids all who crave the warm embrace of fame, heroism, and renown to join the revelry. His kind are the young farmers who look over the glade dreaming of bards telling how they vanquished a great foe, the fiddlers who pray someone will play their song in a hundred years’ time, the adventurer who wished everyone knew their name and smiled. Hopes for grand adventure are met with the demise of their loved ones, spurning on their campaign of revenge. Poets are gifted heartbreaks that rattle their core and inspire refrains that will be quoted for generations, the glory and honor of which are indebted to the Spurring Scar forever. From his table, surrounded by heroes, villains, and masters of their time, he shares tales of all who would be the next greats, his voice crystal clear from behind a mirror mask covering a scarred visage.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Infernal Dukes](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=28)

**Edicts** Patron chroniclers and playwrights, perform dramatic entrances and exits, squeeze your connections for all they’re worth, get the last word

**Anathema** Act with modesty or anonymity, perform great deeds without witnesses, let a slight go unrequited

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Valani (The Fireshaker)](/Deities.aspx?ID=486)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 310

Some things are constantly changing, and Valani teaches that an island is the greatest example of major changes. An island can be born from nothing, rising up from boiling waters. Over time, the hardened volcanic rock transforms into an island full of life. A powerful storm or more volcanic activity can wipe away all this life, leaving the island again bare for new change and transformation. Valani teaches embracing these changes and taking them in stride. The only way to find joy is to take each moment for what it is, and embrace all the changes that come. Valani holds great power over natural forces like storms and especially volcanoes. As such, he sees worship from [druids](/Classes.aspx?ID=34), elementalists, and people living on islands vulnerable to major changes from such primal forces. 

Valani himself is a massive [boar](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=372)-headed figure who wears a crown of spiked grass and purple flowers. His muscular body is encased in armor made from natural fibers that’s as tough as star-forged adamantine. Fireshaker is a creature of great emotional range. It is said that his laughter is strong enough to make tropical trees dance and give up their fruits to those in need, but his quickly found rage is so full of wrath that it can cleave peninsulas from their shores and cause island volcanoes to erupt for months on end. When pleased, his natural forces avoid destroying settlements or majorly disrupting lives. When upset, his storms topple homes and volcanic eruptions destroy hunting grounds, but never to such a degree that mortals can’t adapt to a new life, growing and thriving afterward.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Empyreal Lords](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=10)

**Edicts** Encourage change for the sake of rebirth, respect the power of the elements, focus on your own self growth

**Anathema** Refuse to accept changes in yourself or others, repress you own anger or laughter, use the forces of nature for wanton destruction

**Area of Concern**
Change, growth, primal forces, volcanic islands

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Vale (The Court of Ancestors)](/Deities.aspx?ID=551)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

When souls are judged in [Pharasma’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=290) court, the [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher Vale serves as the [Boneyard’s](/Planes.aspx?ID=39) chief prosecutor. They judge mortals on their actions and the impact their actions have on the world, disregarding their thoughts, beliefs, and even intentions. To Vale, a mortal only proves themselves good or evil through deeds enacted and choices made; there is no kernel of innate purity or corruption within a mortal soul, and no change wrought upon the multiverse from the privacy of the heart or mind.

Vale was created when the first wave of the River of Souls crashed against the Boneyard, carrying the cosmic weight of all mortal cultures and the influence their cultures wrought upon their hearts. They are called the Court of Ancestors, as they are the usher of consequences, superstitions, and mortal traditions, gathering and safeguarding knowledge of life on the Universe. They also care for the souls of mortals whose faith was dedicated to concepts or philosophies unrelated to the gods. Their worshippers include storytellers and those currently mourning a great loss, and they construct temples or pray to the usher in archives, courthouses, next to gallows, and before their hearths.

**Anathema** Allow intent to sway your judgment of an action, disrespect the traditions of those around you

Consequences, superstition, tradition

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Vapula (The Exchequer)](/Deities.aspx?ID=532)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 314

With a greed that rivals that of the oldest [dragons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=395), Vapula relishes knowledge. He particularly savors the moment when one learns something new and has to recontextualize everything as their reality changes. In the chase for revelation, he has acquired quite the collection and developed a knack for cataloging and security. All that is lost is found in his vaults. The prayers of the widower who lost his ring, the pup whose human forgot them, the knight whose sword was knocked into the crevasse in their most dire hour—their quiet offers cross the Keeper of the Pyrite Vault’s ears before any others. For easy favors, wishes can come true. [Devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=389), [demons](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=387), archmagi, and scores of [angels](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=359) come to account with Vapula, each knowing any treasures or threats they deposit are safe and accounted for. Threats from [Asmodeus](/Deities.aspx?ID=278) himself could not ply Vapula, for the Exchequer’s word is his bond, and he is all the more respected for it. Those that meet with Vapula encounter a living stone statue of a horned man wearing an elegant robe, his visage changing every time one looks away.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Infernal Dukes](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=28)

Discovery, hubris, scholars

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Varg (The Iron Warrior)](/Deities.aspx?ID=561)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 318

Varg is another of the older orc deities and is said to be the first [orc](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=66) to learn how to forge blades. In life, Varg was a notably intelligent orc who focused exclusively on waging war. He recognized that the orcs’ enemies were better equipped, better trained, and used better tactics in battle. He sought to learn these things, which allowed him to become a prestigious warlord. However, Varg’s experience in combat was against other orcs. His overconfidence led him to lay “siege” to a walled city outside Belkzen. The siege didn’t last long. In fact, Varg died quickly and his hold scattered.

Before every battle, Varg was known to declare his Deathright. When he succeeded at his Crucible, he spent a great deal of time studying mortals and how they waged war. Siege engines caught his attention, and he gave the secrets of building them to his mortal brethren. Orcs often use these weapons of war to pay homage to the Iron Warrior, but a number see the use of technology for anything other than combat as blasphemy.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Orc Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=29)

**Edicts** Use tactics rather than relying solely on brute force or overwhelming numbers, use siege engines for combat whenever possible, seek out new technology

**Anathema** Pursue technology for non-combat purposes, use machinery and other advanced technology outside of combat, keep advanced weaponry or battle tactics a secret from orcs

Innovation, iron, tactics, technology, war

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Standard">[Vavaalrav (The Steeple’s Skull)](/Deities.aspx?ID=552)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 316

Mortals have always needed ways to remember and honor their ancestors, and it was from this fundamental need the [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher Vavaalrav first imagined the spires and steeples of the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39). Vavaalrav is the guardian of sacred places, and the chill of his breath and stillness of his presence is felt across every mausoleum, tomb, and other burial ground of [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). The Steeple’s Skull does not tolerate when the sanctity of a holy site or the rest of the dead is disturbed, and his symbol is used by mortals to ward graves against foul spirits and grave robbers alike.

The psychopomp’s cult attracts mortal architects, groundskeepers, mortuary workers, and masons, as well as many gargoyles. Even when they don’t worship the usher of graves, [gargoyles](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=49) whose perches adorn cathedrals, temples, and tombs pay Vavaalrav the respect he is due as patron and protector of the hallowed grounds they call home.

Vavaalrav’s home, the Wailing Tor, is an impressive spire at the center of the Boneyard’s Eight Courts. Within its walls, all souls find the peace and rest of the afterlife, and the usher takes special care to welcome and watch over spirits who struggled to accept their fate and leave their mortal lives behind.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Monitor Demigods
](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=12)

**Edicts** Create and erect grave markers, lay bodies to rest, protect graveyards and sacred grounds from despoilment and supernatural threats

**Anathema** Treat grave sites irreverently, allow others to despoil the dead or rob a grave, create undead, desecrate a corpse

Gargoyles, holy ground, rest

Mortals have always needed ways to remember and honor their ancestors, and it was from this fundamental need the [psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=458) usher Vavaalrav first imagined the spires and steeples of the [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=39). Vavaalrav is the guardian of sacred places, and the chill of his breath and stillness of his presence is felt across every mausoleum, tomb, and other burial ground of [the Universe](/Planes.aspx?ID=26). The Steeple’s Skull does not tolerate when the sanctity of a holy site or the rest of the dead is disturbed, and his symbol is used by mortals to ward graves against foul spirits and grave robbers alike.

The psychopomp’s cult attracts mortal architects, groundskeepers, mortuary workers, and masons, as well as many gargoyles. Even when they don’t worship the usher of graves, [gargoyles](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=49) whose perches adorn cathedrals, temples, and tombs pay Vavaalrav the respect he is due as patron and protector of the hallowed grounds they call home.

Vavaalrav’s home, the Wailing Tor, is an impressive spire at the center of the Boneyard’s Eight Courts. Within its walls, all souls find the peace and rest of the afterlife, and the usher takes special care to welcome and watch over spirits who struggled to accept their fate and leave their mortal lives behind.

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 320

Many an idealist with great hopes to change the world has had their dreams realized by meeting a handsome stranger on the road. Velgaas, who might be mistaken for a [nagaji](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=54) with his scaled skin and forked tongue, takes great care to learn their altruistic desires, then carefully plants the seeds of destruction into their kind hearts. Charities become cesspools of corruption, laboratories convert into dens of torture, and peaceful protests spiral into mob violence. 

Velgaas is the most methodical of the sahkil tormentors, preying on good intentions to fulfill his own evil designs. He rules over the aspects of emotional manipulation, emptiness, and ignorance, carefully selecting each word and action to best ingratiate himself with an unsuspecting victim. A honeyed tongue is his weapon, a mask of sincerity his shield. Few of the unfortunate souls who cross his path would ever believe how deeply he’s manipulated them. 

Corrupt politicians and courtiers are among Velgaas’s followers, but he prizes most the ones who fall into his hands unknowingly. The well-meaning authorities he influences might crack down on crime by way of an oppressive city guard or falsify evidence to finally execute a dangerous criminal.

**Category** [Sakhil Tormentors](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=31)

**Edicts** Be sweet with lies and cruel with truths, corrupt the good intentions of others, master the art of manipulation

**Anathema** Be obvious with your lies, reveal the truth without benefit

Emotional manipulation, emptiness, ignorance

<title level="1" right="Deity " pfs="Restricted">[Venkelvore (Most Glorious Neverfull)](/Deities.aspx?ID=506)</title>

<row gap="medium">
<column gap="medium" flex="1 1 400px">

<traits>

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 312

Among [goblins](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=62), Venkelvore is considered the most beautiful of gods. Many goblins depict her as a fellow goblin rather than her true form: a [barghest](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=11) with pale blue fur and a trio of tails. Venkelvore has an eternal hunger that’s only satiated by consuming her enemies. She prefers to eat her meals while still alive, as she not only feeds on the meat but also the prey’s suffering, which Venkelvore considers a fantastic side dish. 

Among the many ways to venerate Venkelvore, her followers believe that the best way to impress her is by tying up as many prisoners as they can during raids and burning them alive, savoring them as they cook or as part of a celebration once the pillaging ends. Her high priests say that the screams of agony please Venkelvore, who rewards those who follow her with more teeth, or sharpening their teeth and claws, allowing these followers to eat their next meal with greater ease.

Goblins who venerate the Most Glorious Neverfull sometimes worship [Lurlup](/Deities.aspx?ID=504) as well. They dedicate their lives to eating everything they can, trying to satiate the hunger of both of their gods. These voracious individuals tend to live isolated lives, as most other goblins tend to find their habits off-putting.

<column gap="tiny">

**Category** [Goblin Gods](/DeityCategories.aspx?ID=27)

**Edicts** Gain beauty through pain and effort, keep a meal within arms length, torment those you eat

**Anathema** Reject a gift of food, neglect your appearance, starve yourself

**Area of Concern**
Beauty, gluttony, sadism

<row gap="medium">

</traits>

**Source** [Divine Mysteries](/Sources.aspx?ID=234) pg. 306

Verilorn, Lord of Wood, Custodian of Oak and Ash, is a gardener. While some might consider gardening to be a free-flowing form of creation, Verilorn believes his gardens should be orderly and exact above all else. The towering trees that fill his arboretums are precise in their positioning and meticulous in their size and shade. Verilorn knows when a sprout will form into wood with such nicety that even the deities who govern time take inspiration.

A rare few of those who’ve indulged in psychoactive plants have been met with horrifying visions of an old woman made of gnarled vines and roots, her sneering mouth full of fang-like thorns and pollen. Those unfortunate enough to meet Vermilion Mother are stalked in their sleep, choked nightly by her dream of a world overrun by plants and fungi. This sahkil tormentor cares little for those of flesh and blood, only that their bodies make for excellent fertilizer.

The Endless Root is worshipped by creatures with a strong preference for nature over civilization, pointing to industry and urbanization as roots of crime and pollution. She doesn’t care for worship but accepts it as a way to promote growth and propagation, enlisting her followers to protect plant life of all kinds. She is one of the few sahkil tormentors to have followers who don’t live wicked lifestyles, some of them even believing themselves benevolent as they work to keep nature unspoiled. But more often than not, her followers are fanatically devoted to the protection of plants to the point of killing anyone they judge as harmful to their territory, using them as sacrifices to feed the undergrowth.
